stages.title: The exchange publishes its book
stages.body: A replayed Nasdaq day is fed into simex as historical liquidity (owner 0). Each order the matching engine accepts goes out as an ITCH 5.0 Add Order. The market data thread packs up to 1400 bytes of messages into one MoldUDP64 packet and multicasts it.

msgs.name: MoldUDP64 packet
msgs.note: Header 20 bytes, then 4 blocks of 2 + 36. 172 bytes on the wire plus UDP/IP.

stages.where: trader · rx and market data threads
stages.title: The feed handler rebuilds the book
stages.body: The rx thread reads the datagram and checks the sequence number (4,812,331 is the next one expected, so no gap). The market data thread decodes each Add Order, applies it to the order-level store and the price-level book, then sends the two best levels per side to the trading thread as a 64-byte TopOfBook.

msgs.name: TopOfBook
msgs.link: SPSC ring, md thread to trading thread
msgs.note: Host byte order (little-endian x86); never leaves the process.

stages.title: The market maker decides
stages.body: The others' best bid and offer are 3 ticks apart, which meets improve_spread_ticks, so the maker steps one tick inside on both sides. Position is flat, so there is no lean. It wants to buy 100 at 189.51 and sell 100 at 189.52. We follow the bid.

stages.title: Pre-trade risk checks the order
stages.body: Inline on the trading thread: seven compares against the OMS, no locks and no calls out. Every check uses integer Price(4) arithmetic except the token bucket.

stages.title: The order leaves the firm
stages.body: The trading thread pushes a 64-byte OrderRequest. The order entry thread, the only one that makes syscalls, encodes OUCH Enter Order, wraps it in SoupBinTCP and writes it to the socket. Tick-to-wire is measured here, from the packet's rx_tsc to this send.

msgs.name: OrderRequest
msgs.link: SPSC ring, trading thread to order entry thread
msgs.note: Host byte order. The OMS has already marked the order pending-new and counted its 100 shares as open buy exposure.
fields: rdtsc of the packet that caused it

msgs.name: SoupBinTCP Unsequenced Data + OUCH Enter Order
msgs.note: 3-byte SoupBinTCP header, then the 47-byte OUCH message. Big-endian integers, space-padded alphas.

stages.title: simex accepts the order and it rests
stages.body: The gateway decodes the Enter Order and pushes a 64-byte Command. The matching thread gives it sequence 9120044, finds nothing to cross at 189.51 (best offer 189.53), and rests it at the front of a new best bid. Two things go out: Order Accepted to the firm, and an Add Order on the public feed.

msgs.name: Command
msgs.link: SPSC ring, gateway thread to matching thread
msgs.note: simex's own 64-byte command; the matcher stamps seq and the journal records it, so every run replays exactly.

msgs.name: SoupBinTCP Sequenced Data + OUCH Order Accepted
msgs.note: Sequenced: both sides count Soup S packets, so a reconnect replays from the next number.

msgs.name: ITCH Add Order (the firm's bid, public)
msgs.note: Anonymous: the feed shows the order reference number, never the account.

stages.title: A FIX firm sells into the bid
stages.body: Another firm trades over FIX 4.4. fixgw checks the session sequence (217), validates the tags, indexes the ClOrdID and maps the order onto an OUCH Enter Order on its own SoupBinTCP session to simex.

msgs.name: FIX NewOrderSingle (35=D)
msgs.note: tag=value, SOH-delimited (shown as |). 9 is the byte count after it up to 10=; 10 is the byte sum mod 256.

msgs.name: SoupBinTCP + OUCH Enter Order (from fixgw)
msgs.note: 54=2 becomes Side S, 44=189.51 becomes 1895100, 11 is copied into ClOrdID. UserRefNum continues from the base the Account Query gave fixgw.

stages.title: The engine matches
stages.body: The sell at 189.51 crosses the firm's resting bid. Price-time priority: the resting order sets the price, 189.51. The firm's order is fully filled and leaves the book. One execution fans out into four messages: two OUCH Order Executed, one ITCH Order Executed and one drop copy report.

msgs.name: SoupBinTCP + OUCH Order Executed (to the firm)
msgs.note: Liquidity A: the firm's order was resting, so it added liquidity. fixgw gets the same message with its own UserRefNum and flag R.

msgs.name: ITCH Order Executed (public)
msgs.note: Every feed handler takes 100 shares off order 5. The match number is the same one the two firms see.

msgs.name: SoupBinTCP + Drop Copy Execution Report
msgs.link: TCP to DROP01, the back office
msgs.note: Independent of the trading session, so the back office can reconcile what the trader believes.

stages.where: fixgw → FIX firm · trader OMS · post-trade
stages.title: Both firms book the fill
stages.body: The FIX firm gets an ExecutionReport. The firm's order entry thread decodes Order Executed into a 64-byte OrderResponse; the OMS turns pending exposure into a position. The quote is now lopsided (long 100), so the next quote leans down a tick. After the run, research/report.py joins trader fills and drop copy on match number: they must agree exactly.

msgs.name: FIX ExecutionReport (35=8, 150=F)
msgs.note: fixgw turns OUCH Order Executed into ExecType F (trade), OrdStatus 2 (filled), with LastQty/LastPx and running CumQty/AvgPx. It is stored for resend in case FIXB reconnects.

msgs.name: OrderResponse
msgs.link: SPSC ring, order entry thread to trading thread
fields: rdtsc when the OUCH packet arrived
